classification.difficultyReason: Separate the inclusive pair counts from the triple overlap, choose an order for using the three complement totals to recover the remaining regions, then reconstruct the sample size for the probability.

inlines.text: The Venn diagram below depicts the investment choices from a random sample of people. Every person invests in at least one of these ways: shares, real estate or interest from a bank account.

The following information was gathered. 320 did not want to buy real estate, 500 would not invest through bank account interest, 385 would not invest in shares, 240 invest in shares and real estate, 205 invest through shares and bank interest, 45 invest only through bank interest, and 110 invest using all three methods.
Find the probability that a randomly chosen person invests in shares.

spec.sourceRegion: Problem 2, between the investment context and the data paragraph
spec.description: Blank three-circle Venn diagram with Shares above Real Estate and Interest, enclosed by a universal rectangle.
spec.mathematics: All seven interior regions and the exterior are present. The regions contain no counts.

inlines.text: The four regions inside the Shares circle contain 515 of the 900 people.

answer.worked:
Put 110 in the central overlap and 45 in the Interest-only region. The exterior count is 0 because everyone uses at least one method.

Subtract the central overlap from each given pairwise count.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Shares and real estate only}&=240-110\\\text{Shares and real estate only}&=130\\\text{Shares and interest only}&=205-110\\\text{Shares and interest only}&=95\end{align*}$$

Use the counts outside each named circle to fill the remaining regions. Outside Real Estate there are shares only, shares and interest only, and interest only. Outside Interest there are shares only, shares and real estate only, and real estate only. Outside Shares there are real estate only, interest only, and real estate and interest only.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Shares only}&=320-95-45\\\text{Shares only}&=180\\\text{Real estate only}&=500-180-130\\\text{Real estate only}&=190\\\text{Real estate and interest only}&=385-190-45\\\text{Real estate and interest only}&=150\end{align*}$$

Add the four regions inside Shares, then include the 385 people outside Shares to find the sample size.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Number investing in shares}&=180+130+95+110\\\text{Number investing in shares}&=515\\\text{Sample size}&=515+385\\\text{Sample size}&=900\\P(\text{invests in shares})&=\frac{515}{900}\\P(\text{invests in shares})&=\frac{103}{180}\end{align*}$$
